topic: Measures of disease frequency and association
title: Incidence, prevalence and relative risk
instructions:
## Counting disease in a district

A district of **50,000** people recorded **400 new** cases of a disease in a year; **1,200** people had the disease at mid-year; **20** of the new cases died. In a cohort study, **30 of 300** exposed people and **10 of 500** unexposed people fell ill.

1. The incidence rate per 1,000 per year.
2. The point prevalence per 1,000 at mid-year.
3. The case fatality as a percentage.
4. The relative risk of exposure.
5. The attributable risk per 100 exposed.
hints: Incidence = new cases / population at risk; prevalence = existing cases / population.
Relative risk = risk in exposed ÷ risk in unexposed = (30/300) ÷ (10/500).
Attributable risk = risk in exposed − risk in unexposed.
realityNote: District Health Information System (DHIS2) reports in Ghana compute exactly these per-1,000 and per-100,000 rates; the denominator (population at risk) is usually the hardest number to get right.
